menuPauseSection.title: Pausing from the in-game Menu
paragraphs: While Menu, Settings, Jukebox, Save, or Load is open from within a running game, automation and background visual effects stop. A GAME PAUSED status appears in the Menu.

When Menu closes, the simulation resumes from the same moment and does not process the time spent paused. Disable this option under Settings > General if automation and background visual effects should continue while you navigate the Menu.

Paused Menu time is excluded from total play time. Resource regeneration timers, research timers, autosaves, and delayed game events do not advance; saving from a paused Menu preserves the same frozen game clock.

fullWelcome.title: Thank you for buying Realindustry
fullWelcome.subtitle: Before your first shift on NIZ-08, I want to say something plainly.
thanksParagraphs: Realindustry was built by one developer over years of research, redesigns, late nights, mistakes, and stubborn care for industrial detail. Your purchase is not just a sale number. It helps this strange independent project keep breathing.
Thank you for trusting a quiet, demanding game about production chains, real materials, automation, and the uncomfortable question of what efficiency does to people when nobody stops to ask why.
fullWelcome.journeyBody: You begin with wood, stone, and hand tools, then climb through metallurgy, chemistry, electricity, electronics, nuclear systems, quantum components, and the Hyperdrive Engine. Most of it is grounded in real industrial logic; the fiction grows out of that machinery instead of replacing it.
fullWelcome.depthBody: The colony will give you objectives. The interface will give you numbers. But Realindustry also hides story in wording, records, terminal fragments, archived endings, and the things the system says too cleanly. Some answers are easy to miss if you only optimize.
fullWelcome.endingBody: There are endings you can reach by finishing the assignment, and there is a deeper end that asks much more from you. Reaching it means paying attention, questioning comfortable instructions, and following threads that may not look like progress at first.
fullWelcome.closingBody: Good luck, Director. Build carefully. Read what is left behind. And thank you for giving this world your time.

stats.productionBlocksElectronic: Shows reachable Production blocks / unlocked slot limit. Every Production block occupies a slot even while disabled; enabling more blocks also increases the automation power cost applied to each production cycle. Raise this limit in the building’s electronic automation console under “{{upgrades}}” with “{{upgrade}}”.
stats.productionBlocksManual: Shows every reachable Production block in the scheme. There is no block limit, but active blocks determine how many colonists and Rest blocks the scheme needs.
stats.maxIterationsElectronic: The largest batch allowed in one Production block. Iterations multiply that block’s inputs and outputs; each extra iteration also raises its electronic automation energy cost. Raise this limit in the building’s electronic automation console under “{{upgrades}}” with “{{upgrade}}”.
stats.maxIterationsManual: Manual blocks may use up to 9,999 iterations. On each uninterrupted linear section, the iterations of all active Production blocks are added together and require one colonist per five iterations, rounded up.
stats.colonists: Now / Max / Available. “Now” counts enabled Production blocks; “Max” assumes every Production block is enabled. Staffing is calculated separately for each uninterrupted linear section: one colonist per five total iterations, rounded up, then the sections are added.
stats.restBlocks: Reachable Rest blocks / minimum required for the currently enabled production: one Rest block per two assigned colonists, rounded up. Every closed production cycle must also contain enough Rest blocks for the colonists working inside that cycle.

templates.standardManual: The simplest ready-made closed loop: one Production block followed by a Rest block. Use it for one routine recipe, then adjust the recipe and iteration count.
templates.sequentialManual: Four Production blocks run one after another on a single uninterrupted route, followed by two Rest blocks. Their iterations are pooled before staffing is calculated, so this template minimizes colonists when tasks can be performed sequentially.
templates.parallelManual: Four independent closed loops start at once. This gives the best simultaneous throughput when enough colonists are free, but each branch is staffed separately and has its own Rest block, so it usually uses more colonists than the sequential template.
templates.standardElectronic: The simplest electronic closed loop: one Production block repeats indefinitely. It is the clearest starting point for a routine recipe or a small custom scheme.
templates.sequentialElectronic: Four Production blocks repeat in a fixed order inside one loop. Use it when later recipes must wait for earlier ones; the blocks do not overlap, but all four still count toward the slot limit and the electronic power multiplier.
templates.parallelElectronic: Four independent closed loops start together and produce simultaneously. It is usually the fastest option when slots and power are available, but it requires four production slots and active blocks raise electronic energy use.
templates.standardConditional: Runs two inventory checks in parallel. Production begins only when both checks are true; if either is false, the scheme waits briefly and retries. Use it when a recipe must be guarded by two prerequisites.
templates.complexSequential: An advanced four-production loop with success and error routes that rejoin at different stages. Use it when recipes must run in order and failures should trigger alternate production; review every recipe and error connection before launch.
templates.complexConditional: Combines two parallel conditions, a Barrier, a five-pass inner loop with two parallel productions, and a fallback production route. It demonstrates nested control flow and recovery paths, but needs all four production slots and careful recipe setup.
templates.parallelConditional: Starts four independent conditional controllers at once. Each branch has its own two-condition gate, wait-and-retry route, and production loop. It offers high autonomy and throughput, but requires four slots, more power, and the most setup work.

blocks.start: The only entry point of a scheme; exactly one Start block is required and it must have an outgoing connection. When an enabled scheme has no active tasks or waiting Barrier signals, execution begins here again.
blocks.end: Stops only the execution branch that reaches it; other branches keep running. Once no active tasks or signals waiting at a Barrier remain, the whole scheme switches off automatically and does not restart from Start on its own. Place it on finite exits where execution should end.
blocks.productionElectronic: Runs the selected recipe for the chosen number of iterations whenever a signal arrives. After its timer completes, it consumes inputs, fuel, tools, and automation power and creates the outputs. “Next” is used on success; “Error” handles an invalid recipe or missing resources, otherwise the block waits until the problem is resolved.
blocks.productionManual: Runs the selected recipe for the chosen number of iterations whenever a signal arrives, at twice the base production time. On one uninterrupted linear section, all active Production iterations are pooled and cost one colonist per five iterations, rounded up. Disabling the block skips it and releases its staffing cost.
blocks.wait: Pauses only the arriving execution branch for 1–3,600 seconds, then forwards it through “Next”. Use it to throttle retries or space out production. In colonist automation it does not split a linear staffing section.
blocks.rest: A fixed five-second recovery stop available only to colonist automation. The scheme needs one reachable Rest block per two assigned colonists, rounded up, and every closed production cycle must independently contain enough rest. Rest does not split a linear staffing section.
blocks.loop: Sends execution through “Loop” the chosen number of times, then through “Exit”; 0 means endless repetition and never uses Exit. The loop body must connect back to this Loop block to repeat. Loop is a control-flow boundary and starts a new colonist staffing section.
blocks.condition: Instantly compares the current inventory amount of one resource with the chosen threshold and follows either “True” or “False”. Both outputs must be connected. It is electronic-only and is useful before production, wait/retry paths, or alternate routes.
blocks.split: Copies one incoming signal to every connected branch, so 2–8 routes proceed independently and can run simultaneously. Use a Barrier later if all branches must finish before continuing; a Joiner will not wait. In colonist automation, Splitter starts separate staffing sections.
blocks.join: Merges several possible routes into one output without synchronization: every arriving signal immediately produces its own “Next” signal. Use it to reunite alternatives or return paths. To wait for all parallel branches, use a Barrier instead; Joiner also breaks colonist staffing sections.
blocks.barrier: Waits until every connected input has received a signal, consumes one signal from each input, then emits a single “Next” signal; extra arrivals remain queued for later sets. Place it after parallel branches that must all finish. Barrier is electronic-only.
blocks.reroute: A visual routing point that bends long or crossing connections without changing execution. A signal entering one side leaves through the opposite side, and it does not split a colonist staffing section. Drag it to tidy the graph; double-click it to remove it.
